analysis.title: China's bear market: too broken to buy, too oversold to short
key_insights: CSI 300 is in a bear market, down 20% from its June peak after 10 consecutive weekly declines. The sell-off accelerated after the late-August death cross, driven by the global AI unwind, fading stimulus hopes and weak domestic fundamentals.
Better-than-expected Q3 GDP did not lift sentiment, and rising oil prices add a headwind. The 4,000 level on the CSI 300 is the next level to watch, with little urgency to buy China.
CSI 300 is at its most oversold level in the history of the data series. The trend remains bearish, but the risk of a sharp countertrend squeeze is growing.
HSTECH fell 5% overnight and continues to trade inside a downward trend channel in place since last year. The 100- and 200-day moving averages are far above current levels.
The performance gap between Chinese and US tech has reached extreme levels.
Consensus 2026 earnings growth for MSCI China has fallen from more than 11% at the start of the year to about 1%, according to BofA.

BofA argues that national-team buying, buybacks, liquidity injections and limits on institutional selling are more likely to set a floor than start a sustained rally. The average one-month CSI 300 gain after the past 29 RRR cuts was about 1%.
China's economy is split. Exports and industrial production continue to grow, while domestic consumption is weak and real estate investment keeps falling (JPM).
New home sales are roughly 40% of their 2019 level even as real retail sales rise (GS).
Chinese households hold an estimated RMB 63 trillion in excess bank deposits and the savings rate is 33.4%, yet consumption disappoints (GS).
Household short-term loan flows are deeply negative and longer-term borrowing is very weak, so household deleveraging continues despite Beijing's efforts (GS).
Chinese equities have tracked inverted oil closely, so surging energy prices are another headwind.
Southbound flows flipped from net buying to net selling last week and trading activity is subdued, leaving no clear marginal buyer (BofA).

sector_views.rationale: HSTECH is in a persistent bear trend channel, far below its 100- and 200-day moving averages, and has underperformed US tech by an extreme margin.

earnings_insights: BofA: consensus 2026 earnings growth for MSCI China has fallen from more than 11% at the start of the year to barely 1% (consensus estimate, not a reported figure).

macro_indicators.interpretation: The beat did not improve equity sentiment, which is being driven by AI unwind, weak stimulus and domestic fundamentals.
High savings with weak consumption points to low willingness to spend (GS).
Ample household liquidity that is not being spent (GS).
The property downturn remains the biggest structural drag on domestic demand (GS).

risk_factors: Further decline toward 4,000 on the CSI 300.
Rising oil prices, which have been inversely correlated with Chinese equities.
Falling earnings expectations for MSCI China.
Weak household consumption and borrowing, and the property slump.
Policy support that sets a floor but does not start a rally.
Counter-risk: a sharp short squeeze from extreme oversold levels.

tension_points.bull_case: CSI 300 is at its most oversold level in the history of the data, and a violent countertrend squeeze risk is growing. National-team buying and policy support may set a floor.
tension_points.bear_case: The trend is firmly bearish, MSCI China 2026 earnings growth has fallen to about 1%, southbound flows turned to net selling, domestic demand is weak, and policy easing has historically produced only about a 1% one-month gain.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break below 4,000 on the CSI 300 would extend the bear case.
